title: Handle SSL.Error during TLS version context setup in is_supported_version
answers: Why does mitmproxy crash with SSL.Error during TLS option validation?
How to handle OpenSSL builds rejecting removed TLS protocols at context setup?
What causes unhandled SSL.Error in is_supported_version on OpenSSL builds without SSLv3?
body:
Symptom: Crash with unhandled SSL.Error during TLS option validation on OpenSSL environments that have dropped legacy protocol support.
Root cause: mitmproxy/net/tls.py:is_supported_version set protocol versions and initialized SSL.Connection outside the guarded try/except block.
Fix pattern: Move protocol-version context setters and connection initialization inside the try/except SSL.Error block so setup failures return False instead of raising.
Constraints: Applies when probing protocol support via pyOpenSSL where removed or disabled versions fail during context configuration rather than I/O probing.
says: The application crashes on startup when validating secure connection settings on newer operating systems.
Proxy terminates unexpectedly when configuring secure protocol versions on modern security libraries.
Opening TLS settings crashes if legacy encryption protocols are not supported by the system.
Prevent proxy crashes when older encryption versions are disabled on the host machine.
